titlePlain: Writing the T-SQL Query That Defines
subtitle: Video 7 of 22 · Northfield Retail

code:
DECLARE @AsOfDate DATE = '2026-09-30';
-- swap for GETDATE() in production
caption: One variable makes the whole query re-runnable against history.

code:
WITH LastPurchase AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, MAX(OrderDate) AS LastOrderDate
  FROM Sales.Orders
  WHERE OrderTotal > 0        -- excludes returns/refunds
  GROUP BY CustomerID
),
PriorYearPurchaseCount AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount12Mo
  FROM Sales.Orders
  WHERE OrderTotal > 0
    AND OrderDate >= DATEADD(MONTH, -12, @AsOfDate)
    AND OrderDate <  @AsOfDate
  GROUP BY CustomerID
)
caption: Last purchase date, and the trailing-12-month count.

code:
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.Region, c.Segment,
  CASE
    WHEN lp.LastOrderDate IS NULL THEN 'Never Purchased'
    WHEN DATEDIFF(DAY,lp.LastOrderDate,@AsOfDate)<=90
      THEN 'Active'
    WHEN DATEDIFF(DAY,lp.LastOrderDate,@AsOfDate)>90
      AND ISNULL(py.PurchaseCount12Mo,0)>=2
      THEN 'Churned'
    ELSE 'Not Yet Retained'
  END AS CustomerStatus
FROM Sales.Customers c
LEFT JOIN LastPurchase lp ON lp.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
LEFT JOIN PriorYearPurchaseCount py ON py.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE c.Segment <> 'Wholesale';
caption: One row per customer — LEFT JOINs so zero-order customers still appear.
